title: The old sage weeps
hookLine: the sage Asita holds the baby, smiles, then weeps: he will not live to hear this child teach
last: LUMBINI — BORN ON THE WAY SOMEWHERE.

lines: AN OLD SEER HURRIES TO THE PALACE.
cards: Gods in the sky, the story says, celebrating: waving their cloaks, shouting for joy. An old seer named Asita, resting in his daytime retreat, sees them and asks why.
They tell him: in the land of the Sakyas, a child has been born who will one day turn the wheel of the teaching. So the old man hurries to King Suddhodana's palace and asks to see the baby.
The king brings the child out, and Asita takes him in his arms.

teach.b: This story is told in verse, in a collection called the Sutta Nipata. Asita holds the baby and looks at him closely, the way an expert looks at something rare. He reads the marks on the child's body, and he's sure.
Joyful, he lifts his voice: this one is supreme, the highest among people. Then, holding the child, the old man starts to cry. The Sakyans are frightened.
Is something wrong with the baby? Is danger coming? No, Asita tells them.
Nothing bad will happen to this child. He'll reach the highest awakening, teach out of compassion for many, and his way of life will spread far. I'm weeping for myself.

teach.h: I WON'T LIVE TO HEAR HIM.
teach.b: I'll be gone before he teaches, and I won't be there to hear it. It's a strange, tender moment this early in the story: the one who sees clearly who this child is knows he'll never see it come true.
He goes to his nephew, a young man named Nalaka, and tells him: when you hear that someone has awakened and is teaching, go to him.
Follow him. Years later, the story says, Nalaka does. The old man couldn't reach the future himself, so he sent someone into it: a seed planted in a garden he knew he'd never walk in.

how: Buddhists tell the story of Asita as part of the Buddha's birth, and in Theravada communities the Nalaka Sutta is recited and studied; the scene of Asita holding the infant appears in temple art across Asia.

the old seer who held the baby and wept
a hermit who warned the king of danger

he wept for himself: he would die before the child taught.
this story is told in verse in the Sutta Nipata
in the Nalaka Sutta, with Asita and his nephew.
Asita told his nephew to follow the child when he began teaching

games.q: you're Asita. you've just held the child and you know you'll die before he teaches. what do you do?
o: hide your tears and go home.
tell your nephew to follow him when the time comes.
stay at the palace to wait.
games.why: he tells his nephew Nalaka: when you hear he's awakened, go to him. the old man couldn't reach the future, so he sent someone into it.

practice: Bring to mind a good thing you won't see finished: a tree you planted, a child or student you won't see grown, a cause longer than your life, a kindness rippling somewhere you'll never know.
Hold it the way Asita held the child, close and with open hands. If sadness and joy both come, let both be there.

wordCard.voice: Asita. The old seer who held the newborn, knew who he'd become, wept because he wouldn't live to hear him teach, and sent his nephew instead.

orig.note: Pali and Sanskrit: a name meaning dark or black (a- + sita, white).

carryVoice: Your line: plant it anyway, even in a garden you won't walk in. That's day twenty-four.
